title: Fragmented payload synthesis and loss-mitigation protocol for streamed structured outputs
creator: Hannah Ortiz
description:
Problem summary: When the API streams structured objects (JSON) while also supporting tool/function calling and compatibility fallbacks, we observe frequent partial-object emission due to truncation, tokenization boundaries, and intermediate escapes inserted by models. Current heuristics (sequence numbers + naive bracket balancing) fail for nested objects and for toolcall payloads that include embedded JSON strings. Users get corrupted tool arguments or invalid JSON which breaks downstream tool runtimes or client-side parsers.

Goal: Design and implement a robust, backward-compatible protocol and runtime implementation to synthesize fragmented object payloads, mitigate loss from truncation, and provide deterministic retry/repair semantics for idempotent tool/function calls. The protocol must: 1) be integrable without client SDK changes for the majority of callers, 2) provide an opt-in stricter framing mode for advanced clients, 3) allow graceful degradation to line-delimited NDJSON for very old clients, and 4) instrument key observability signals for regressions.

Proposed approach (high level):
- Chunk manifest headers: Add an optional lightweight envelope header per stream chunk containing: manifest_id, chunk_index, chunk_count (if known), crc32, payload_type (object_fragment | text | toolcall), and optional boundary_hint (string). Envelope encoded as a single-line prefix using a compact header token that clients can ignore if unrecognized (backwards compatible). Example prefix: "~RWD/1 manifest=abc123 idx=2/5 crc=1f2d payload=object_fragment hint=arr_end"
- Fragment semantics: Emit fragments that align to logical token boundaries when possible. Each fragment marked object_fragment includes a boundary_hint that indicates whether the fragment ends on a probable field boundary, value boundary, or is mid-token. Runtime will favor inserting escape scaffolding instead of unbalanced braces when termination is imminent.
- Checkpoint/backfill: Maintain server-side per-manifest checkpoint window for 30s allowing subsequent requests (from same client session or via replay) to request missing chunk_index ranges. API will expose a resume endpoint: POST /v1/resume_stream with manifest_id and observed_chunk_indices. Server replies with missing fragments and a reconciliation diff (NDJSON of operations) to reconstruct full object.
- Repair heuristics: On clients that cannot use resume, implement best-effort reconstruction rules: 1) attempt bracket balancing with token-aware backtracking, 2) prefer inserting closing braces rather than removing trailing tokens, 3) use boundary_hint hints when present, 4) when toolcall payloads are malformed, attempt to extract top-level fields using regex heuristics and reparsable substrings.
- Idempotent toolcalls: For function/tool call events, attach a call_id UUID in the manifest header. If a toolcall completes on server then manifest is recorded; retries with same call_id must be treated idempotently by runtime and downstream tool routing. Document semantics for at-most-once vs at-least-once depending on customer-configured retry_policy.
- Opt-in strict framing: Provide header mode "framing=strict-v1" which wraps each object in length-prefixed framing for clients that prefer correctness over streaming latency. This mode will be disabled by default to preserve current SDK behavior.

Trade-offs and rationale:
- Envelope header size adds ~40-80 bytes per chunk; trade-off versus fewer corrupted payloads is acceptable for P0 customer impact.
- Checkpoint window retention increases server state; we limit to 30s by default and make it configurable per-release tier. Longer retention for Dedicated/Private customers available.
- Resume endpoint introduces extra roundtrip; chosen as a targeted fix for high-value toolcalls rather than default path for all streams.

Instrumentation and observability:
- New metrics: stream_manifest_creation_rate, manifest_replay_rate, fragment_repair_rate, fragment_truncation_rate, toolcall_idempotent_conflicts, resume_success_rate.
- Logs: Structured log entry on manifest finalization including sizes, chunk_count, and any repair action taken. Correlate with request_id and call_id.
- Dashboards: console-2026.03 -> Structured Output -> Fragment Repair to show top-level customers and models causing most fragmentation.

Testing plan:
- Unit tests for envelope parsing, checksum validation, and repair heuristics.
- Integration tests mocking partial token streams using recorded model tokenization boundaries (use corpora in infra/tests/stream-fixtures).
- Fuzz-testing harness to simulate mid-token truncation, nested quoted JSON in toolcall arguments, and deliberate CRC mismatches.
- E2E test against tool-runner to validate idempotent call handling (github PR hook in runtime: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1234).

Rollout plan:
1) Feature-flag gated server-side implementation (ff:fragmented_payload_heuristics). Deploy to Canary pool (hosted) + Dedicated alpha customers.
2) Collect metrics for 7 days; evaluate repair_rate and resume_success_rate.
3) Opt-in SDK patch in JS/Python that recognizes envelope prefix and exposes resume helpers; gradually flip stricter framing for customers requesting it.
4) GA in runtime-2.4 if metrics indicate >=75% of repairs succeed without manual intervention.

Open questions & next steps:
- Should the manifest_id be globally unique across the entire org or scoped to customer/session? (proposal: UUID v4 per stream, include customer prefix for debugging).
- Exact retention policy for Dedicated customers and edge cases for manual restore requests.
- Standardize CRC algorithm (crc32 vs adler32) for performance.

comments: 2026-03-02 - Arjun Mehta: Initial spike completed. Prototype implements envelope prefix parsing and basic bracket-balancing repair. See PR 1234. Observed ~12% reduction in toolcall failures in canary. Needs fuzzing and resume endpoint.

2026-03-04 - Priya Kapoor (PM): We should align on UX for SDK resume helpers. If we expose resume API, we must ensure rate limits and auth are gated. Prioritize Dedicated customers who reported failures.

2026-03-06 - Miguel Santos (Design): For clients that surface repair to end-users, provide standardized feedback strings and error codes. UX doc linked in Confluence page. Approved approach for default mute of repair details in hosted mode.

2026-03-09 - SRE: Checkpoint retention increased memory by ~2% in canary under synthetic workload; we'll cap manifest retention based on requests/s. Recommending 30s default with feature flag to increase for Dedicated.

2026-03-11 - Arjun Mehta: Added idempotent call_id semantics and updated PR to store manifest final state to durable event log on success. Next: implement resume_endpoint and add tests for toolcall replay safety.
